Question: Convex quadrilateral \(ABCD\) has \(AB = 9\) and \(CD = 12.\) Diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect at \(E,\) \(AC = 14,\) and \(\triangle AED\) and \(\triangle BEC\) have equal areas. What is \(AE?\)
Solution:
Method 1: Add a common triangle

Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of \(\triangle XYZ\). Convexity places \(E\) inside both diagonals and places \(C\) and \(D\) on the same side of line \(AB\).

Adding \([ABE]\) to the given equal areas produces two larger triangles with the same base:
\[
\begin{aligned}
[ABD]&=[ABE]+[AED]\\
&=[ABE]+[BEC]=[ABC].
\end{aligned}
\]
Since these triangles share base \(AB\), they have equal perpendicular heights. Points \(C\) and \(D\) are on the same side of \(AB\), so their equal distances from that line place them on the same parallel to it. Therefore \(CD\parallel AB\).

Now \(\angle ABE=\angle CDE\) by parallel lines, and \(\angle AEB=\angle CED\) because they are vertical angles. Thus \(\triangle AEB\sim\triangle CED\), giving
\[
\frac{AE}{EC}=\frac{AB}{CD}=\frac9{12}=\frac34.
\]
Because \(AE+EC=AC=14\), the segment \(AE\) is three of seven equal parts of \(AC\). Hence
\[
AE=\frac37\cdot14=\boxed{6},
\]
choice E.

Method 2: Compare areas using common heights

Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of \(\triangle XYZ\). Since the quadrilateral is convex, all four diagonal segments and the areas of the triangles around \(E\) are positive.

Compare both given equal areas with \([AEB]\). Triangles \(AED\) and \(AEB\) have bases \(ED\) and \(EB\) on line \(BD\), with the same altitude from \(A\). Similarly, triangles \(BEC\) and \(BEA\) have bases \(EC\) and \(EA\) on line \(AC\), with the same altitude from \(B\). Therefore
\[
\frac{[AED]}{[AEB]}=\frac{ED}{EB},
\qquad
\frac{[BEC]}{[AEB]}=\frac{EC}{EA}.
\]
The given area equality implies
\[
\frac{ED}{EB}=\frac{EC}{EA},
\qquad
\frac{AE}{EC}=\frac{BE}{ED}.
\]
All denominators are positive. These are the ratios of the two sides surrounding \(E\) in triangles \(AEB\) and \(CED\). Their included angles are equal vertical angles, so the triangles are similar by side-angle-side similarity.

Corresponding sides now give
\[
\frac{AE}{EC}=\frac{AB}{CD}=\frac9{12}=\frac34.
\]
Since \(AE+EC=14\),
\[
AE=\frac3{3+4}\cdot14=\boxed{6},
\]
choice E.
